evidence_chain.link: The mention of inspiratory stridor in the context of epiglottitis, which can be caused by viral or bacterial infections, suggests that B1 is a plausible candidate.
evidence_chain.quote: Epiglottitis is suspected in patients with severe sore throat and no pharyngitis and also in patients with sore throat and inspiratory stridor.

evidence_chain.link: The description of supraglottitis/epiglottitis does not strongly support B2 as the primary candidate, given the absence of preceding URI symptoms.
evidence_chain.quote: With supraglottitis/epiglottitis, there is abrupt onset of severe throat pain and dysphagia, usually with no preceding URI symptoms.

ranked_facts.why: The presence of inspiratory stridor is more commonly associated with viral upper respiratory infections, such as croup or viral tracheitis, which are included in the B1 candidate. In contrast, bacterial upper respiratory infections, such as those included in B2, may present with different symptoms.
